questions: What is the all-in cost of the Lisbon offsite for 60 people once flights, local transport, insurance and a contingency are added to the 70,000 euro quote?
What items beyond the venue quote must the 10,000 euro remainder cover, and can it?
At what total cost, or number of attendees, would the Lisbon plan go over 80,000 euros?
Could the offsite be a hybrid, with a Lisbon group and others joining remotely?
Does the venue quote cover all 60 people at the expected room and meeting-space needs?
How many of the 60 people have a known reason they cannot travel on the fixed dates?
Are there other locations or formats, such as a cheaper city or a smaller in-person group, that would meet the goal?
Is the venue holding your dates now, and until when can you decide without losing them?
What do the employees themselves want from the offsite, and what would make them use the time well?
What are the deposit and cancellation terms, and at what date would you lose money by backing out?

criteria: Cross-team interaction among the 60 employees is measurably higher afterwards (new cross-team contacts, joint work, post-event survey)
Total cost, including travel, accommodation, and time lost, stays within 80,000 euros
All 60 employees can actually attend on the fixed dates
Participation quality: people are engaged during the event rather than distracted
stated_facts: Dates are fixed by the leadership calendar
Last year's remote offsite was rated poorly

assumptions.text: The 70,000 euro venue quote leaves enough in the budget for everything else it needs to cover.
Last year's poor rating was caused by the remote format rather than by how that event was designed.
Being in the same place automatically produces cross-team collaboration.
All employees are able and willing to travel to Lisbon on the fixed dates.

uncertainties.text: What does the 70,000 euro quote include (rooms, meals, meeting spaces, activities), and what are the extra costs for flights, local transport, insurance, and contingency for 60 people?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the all-in cost stays under 80,000, Lisbon is feasible and favored; if travel and extras push it past the budget, remote or a scaled-down alternative is favored.

uncertainties.text: Can everyone attend in person on the fixed dates, given visas, caregiving, health, and other commitments, and where are people based?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If nearly everyone can travel, Lisbon is favored; if a notable share cannot, in-person splits the group and remote is favored.

uncertainties.text: Why was last year's remote offsite rated poorly: format, length, time zones, content, or poor facilitation?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the problems were inherent to remote, Lisbon is favored; if they were from design flaws that can be fixed, a better remote offsite is viable and cheaper.

uncertainties.text: Is the venue's date availability and cancellation or deposit terms already firm, given the dates are fixed?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the venue is confirmed with flexible terms, Lisbon is lower risk; if the dates are not held or deposits are non-refundable, committing is riskier and remote is favored.

uncertainties.text: Which cross-team collaboration problems need solving (specific team pairs, project handovers), and would structured sessions, rather than location, address them?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If targeted, well-designed sessions are what matters, either format could work and cost decides; if informal in-person time is what is lacking, Lisbon is favored.

uncertainties.text: Could the remaining budget under remote (about 80,000 euros) be spent on something that improves collaboration, such as regional meetups or team-pair visits?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the money can buy better collaboration outcomes in another way, remote plus spending is favored; if not, Lisbon's use of the budget is favored.

chosen.question: What is the all-in cost of the Lisbon offsite for 60 people once flights, local transport, insurance and a contingency are added to the 70,000 euro quote?
chosen.why: If it exceeds the budget, Lisbon is no longer clearly better.
chosen.answer_path: Get flight estimates from your team's home locations, ask the venue for a full breakdown, and total the lines.

chosen.question: What items beyond the venue quote must the 10,000 euro remainder cover, and can it?
chosen.why: Checks whether the quote leaves enough room.
chosen.answer_path: List flights, transport, insurance, activities and contingency and get estimates for each.

chosen.question: At what total cost, or number of attendees, would the Lisbon plan go over 80,000 euros?
chosen.why: Finds the money limit for Lisbon.
chosen.answer_path: Build a cost model by headcount and travel cost and see where it crosses the budget.

chosen.question: Could the offsite be a hybrid, with a Lisbon group and others joining remotely?
chosen.why: The map lists only two pure options.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the venue about hybrid support, and ask teams who would travel.

chosen.question: Does the venue quote cover all 60 people at the expected room and meeting-space needs?
chosen.why: Checks that the quote matches the actual group.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the venue to confirm headcount, room types, and meeting spaces in writing.

chosen.question: How many of the 60 people have a known reason they cannot travel on the fixed dates?
chosen.why: A notable share unable to attend favors remote.
chosen.answer_path: Run a short anonymous survey or ask team leads about visa, caregiving or health constraints.

chosen.question: Are there other locations or formats, such as a cheaper city or a smaller in-person group, that would meet the goal?
chosen.why: Brings in alternatives beyond Lisbon and fully remote.
chosen.answer_path: Request quotes from one or two other venues and compare.

chosen.question: Is the venue holding your dates now, and until when can you decide without losing them?
chosen.answer_path: Ask the venue how long the quote and the date hold last.

chosen.question: What do the employees themselves want from the offsite, and what would make them use the time well?
chosen.why: Employee preferences are not on the map.
chosen.answer_path: Send a short survey asking for preferences and goals.

chosen.question: What are the deposit and cancellation terms, and at what date would you lose money by backing out?
chosen.why: Shows when the Lisbon commitment becomes costly.
chosen.answer_path: Read the venue contract terms and note deadlines for each payment.

candidates.question: What is the all-in cost of the Lisbon offsite for 60 people once flights, local transport, insurance and a contingency are added to the 70,000 euro quote?
candidates.why: If it exceeds the budget, Lisbon is no longer clearly better.
candidates.answer_path: Get flight estimates from your team's home locations, ask the venue for a full breakdown, and total the lines.

candidates.question: How many of the 60 people have a known reason they cannot travel on the fixed dates?
candidates.why: A notable share unable to attend favors remote.
candidates.answer_path: Run a short anonymous survey or ask team leads about visa, caregiving or health constraints.

candidates.question: What did last year's attendees say went wrong, and how many named the remote format itself?
candidates.why: Separates a format problem from a design problem.
candidates.answer_path: Read last year's survey comments and code each complaint by cause.

candidates.question: Which team pairs most need to work better together, and what would change if they spent time together in person?
candidates.why: Targets what collaboration problem the offsite is meant to solve.
candidates.answer_path: Ask team leads for the three weakest handovers and what is missing.

candidates.question: What could you do with the full 80,000 euros under remote that would improve collaboration more than Lisbon?
candidates.why: Compares what each option's money buys.
candidates.answer_path: Sketch two or three alternative uses, such as regional meetups, and cost them.

candidates.question: What items beyond the venue quote must the 10,000 euro remainder cover, and can it?
candidates.why: Checks whether the quote leaves enough room.
candidates.answer_path: List flights, transport, insurance, activities and contingency and get estimates for each.

candidates.question: If last year's event had been designed differently but still remote, what would have gone better?
candidates.why: Checks whether poor ratings came from format or design.
candidates.answer_path: Ask last year's organizers and a sample of attendees what they would change.

candidates.question: At past in-person events, did people from different teams actually mix, or did they stay in their usual groups?
candidates.why: Checks that being in one place produces collaboration.
candidates.answer_path: Ask past organizers and attendees, and look at any photos or survey data.

candidates.question: Are there employees who would be unwilling, rather than unable, to travel, and why?
candidates.why: Willingness is a separate question from ability.
candidates.answer_path: Ask in an anonymous pulse survey, and talk with team leads.

candidates.question: Does the venue quote cover all 60 people at the expected room and meeting-space needs?
candidates.why: Checks that the quote matches the actual group.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the venue to confirm headcount, room types, and meeting spaces in writing.

candidates.question: After a past in-person event, did cross-team work increase in the following weeks, and how would you know?
candidates.why: Tests the cause and effect between co-location and collaboration.
candidates.answer_path: Compare cross-team messages, joint tickets or projects before and after a past event.

candidates.question: Do the remote offsite's low scores line up with specific sessions, times or time zones rather than the format as a whole?
candidates.why: Tests whether remote itself drove the rating.
candidates.answer_path: Break the ratings down by session and by attendee location.

candidates.question: Would planned cross-team sessions, such as joint workshops, produce more interaction than free social time in Lisbon?
candidates.why: Tests which part of the event causes collaboration.
candidates.answer_path: Review research or past agendas, and ask facilitators what drove connections.

candidates.question: Does travel itself, such as long journeys and time away from home, reduce engagement at the event?
candidates.why: Tests whether the in-person format has costs on participation quality.
candidates.answer_path: Check flight times and feedback from past events with travel.

candidates.question: Would smaller regional gatherings produce the same cross-team contacts as one big event?
candidates.why: Tests whether one large event is needed for the effect.
candidates.answer_path: Look at where people live and ask team leads which groups would meet.

candidates.question: At what total cost, or number of attendees, would the Lisbon plan go over 80,000 euros?
candidates.why: Finds the money limit for Lisbon.
candidates.answer_path: Build a cost model by headcount and travel cost and see where it crosses the budget.

candidates.question: How many absences would make an in-person event feel like it splits the company?
candidates.why: Sets a threshold for attendance.
candidates.answer_path: Discuss with leadership and team leads what share absent is acceptable.

candidates.question: What are the deposit and cancellation terms, and at what date would you lose money by backing out?
candidates.why: Shows when the Lisbon commitment becomes costly.
candidates.answer_path: Read the venue contract terms and note deadlines for each payment.

candidates.question: How long could a remote event run before attention drops too far, and what did last year's length look like?
candidates.why: Time limits affect whether remote can work.
candidates.answer_path: Check last year's agenda length and attendance drop-off in the video platform logs.

candidates.question: What happens to the plan if a travel disruption, such as a strike or weather event, affects Lisbon flights on the fixed dates?
candidates.why: Dates are fixed, so disruptions cannot be absorbed by rescheduling.
candidates.answer_path: Check insurance terms, flight options and the venue's force majeure terms.

candidates.question: Could the offsite be a hybrid, with a Lisbon group and others joining remotely?
candidates.why: The map lists only two pure options.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the venue about hybrid support, and ask teams who would travel.

candidates.question: Are there other locations or formats, such as a cheaper city or a smaller in-person group, that would meet the goal?
candidates.why: Brings in alternatives beyond Lisbon and fully remote.
candidates.answer_path: Request quotes from one or two other venues and compare.

candidates.question: What do the employees themselves want from the offsite, and what would make them use the time well?
candidates.why: Employee preferences are not on the map.
candidates.answer_path: Send a short survey asking for preferences and goals.

candidates.question: Is there time to build in follow-up after the offsite so any new connections continue?
candidates.why: Collaboration gains may fade without follow-up.
candidates.answer_path: Ask team leads what follow-up structures they could set up.

candidates.question: What time away from regular work would in-person travel cost the company, and is this counted in the budget?
candidates.why: The goal's budget may not include working time lost.
candidates.answer_path: Estimate travel days per person and check with finance how time is counted.

candidates.question: Is the venue holding your dates now, and until when can you decide without losing them?
candidates.why: Shows the real decision deadline.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the venue how long the quote and the date hold last.

candidates.question: Which choice can you change later if it goes wrong, and which has money or reputation you cannot get back?
candidates.why: Identifies what is hard to undo.
candidates.answer_path: Review deposit rules for Lisbon and what a late switch to remote would cost.

candidates.question: By what date do employees need to know to arrange travel, visas and time off?
candidates.why: Sets a practical deadline.
candidates.answer_path: Check visa processing times and ask HR for notice needed.

candidates.question: Who must approve the final decision and what do they need to see first?
candidates.why: Reduces delay in reaching a decision.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the leadership team what information would settle the matter.

candidates.question: What is your belief that last year's rating was due to remote based on: the survey data, comments you heard, or your own impression?
candidates.why: Separates evidence from impression.
candidates.answer_path: Look at the raw survey results and comments.

candidates.question: How did you decide that the quote leaves enough budget: did you list the other costs or just assume?
candidates.why: Checks the basis of the cost estimate.
candidates.answer_path: Write the full list of costs with estimates and compare.

candidates.question: What is your estimate of how many people can attend based on?
candidates.why: Shows if attendance is known or guessed.
candidates.answer_path: Compare with attendance at previous in-person gatherings.

candidates.question: How do you know that cross-team collaboration is weak now, and which measures or events led you to think so?
candidates.why: Checks the evidence behind the goal's starting point.
candidates.answer_path: Look at available data such as cross-team project counts or survey results.
